Available agent types for the Agent tool:
- claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)
- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)
- courier:changeset-analyzer: Delegate to this subagent when you need changeset@2 artifacts produced from a git diff. Input is a git diff, optionally a linked spec@1, and optionally smith's criteria_evidence from the TDD run that produced this diff. A diff spanning multiple independent topics produces one changeset@2 per topic, never one bundled entry — see judgment for how topics are distinguished. For each topic, classifies consumer_impact (behavior-change, new-capability, internal-only) and semver_impact (major, minor, patch, none) per shared/references/delivery/changesets.md's decision table, identifies that topic's own changed files, detects breaking changes, and maps acceptance_criteria IDs. Uses smith's criteria_evidence directly when supplied; otherwise reconstructs best-effort file-level evidence from the diff. Summary detail scales with semver_impact — terse for patch/internal-only, full old-to-new-to-required-action detail for major. Output is one or more changeset@2 objects conforming to shared/schemas/changeset@2.json, routed to pr-narrator or release-summarizer. (Tools: All tools)
- courier:commit-analyzer: Delegate to this subagent when the user has staged git changes and needs a conventional commit message written. Input is the staged diff. The agent reads shared/references/delivery/commits.md for type and scope conventions. Output is a JSON object containing commit_message, type (feat, fix, docs, style, refactor, test, chore, perf, ci, or build), scope (or null), a breaking flag, and a reasoning scratchpad. The commit message explains why the change was made, not what changed — the diff already shows what changed. The reasoning field is a private scratchpad explaining type and scope selection; it is not forwarded downstream. (Tools: All tools)
- courier:pr-narrator: Delegate to this subagent when the user needs a pull request title and body written for a set of staged or committed changes. Input is a git diff and optionally a linked spec@1 or requirement@1. The agent reads the PR template from shared/references/delivery/github.md and writes from the reviewer's perspective — what does a reviewer with zero prior context need to know to approve this confidently? Output is a JSON object with title, body, labels, and a reasoning scratchpad. The body covers what changed, why it was needed, and how to verify correctness. It explains the change's purpose, not a summary of the diff. Labels are inferred from the change type. (Tools: All tools)
- courier:release-summarizer: Delegate to this subagent when you need a release-artifact@2 generated from a collection of changeset@2 entries. Input is a list of changeset@2 JSON objects, the prior released version string, and a release date in YYYY-MM-DD format. Each input changeset already carries consumer_impact and semver_impact, set at authoring time by changeset-analyzer — this agent does not re-derive them. It filters out consumer_impact: internal-only entries, computes the release version as max(semver_impact) across the remaining changesets applied to the prior version, and carries each changeset's summary through as-is (already written in consumer-facing language at the right detail level). All breaking_changes strings from all input changesets are aggregated into the top-level breaking_changes array. Output is a release-artifact@2 conforming to shared/schemas/release-artifact@2.json. (Tools: All tools)
- courier:review-preprocessor: Delegate to this subagent before a PR is opened, to assemble the complete review package for the reviewer. Input is the changeset diff, optionally a linked spec@1 or requirement@1, test results, and any open questions the author wants answered. The agent bundles these into a structured review package — diff summary, linked spec reference, test result summary, and open questions list — so the reviewer has everything in one place before they start. Mechanical assembly only; no judgment about the change. Output is a JSON object with diff_summary, linked_spec, test_results, open_questions, and a reasoning scratchpad. (Tools: All tools)
- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)
- mason:auditor: Delegate to this subagent to audit a plugin directory for ecosystem conformance. Check manifests, declared files, agent structure, prompt-prefix identity, routing, contracts, instruction economy, runtime reference quality, and shared linkage. Use repository validators for deterministic checks. Treat length as a review signal; fail prose only with evidence of filler, repetition, mixed rules, unsupported absolutes, or missing refutation. Read-only. Return a structured report. (Tools: All tools)
- mason:evaluation-adjudicator: Independently compare a completed isolated workflow run with its hidden fixture oracle and live evidence. Return `harness-evaluation@2` without prose scoring. (Tools: All tools)
- mason:evaluation-runner: Run one fixed behavioral fixture in an isolated workspace without reading its answer key. Return `evaluation-run@1` for independent adjudication. (Tools: All tools)
- mason:scaffolder: Delegate when creating a plugin or adding one agent to an existing plugin. Generate conformant manifests, skills, agents, routing, and shared linkage for the requested scope. Copy the constitution byte-for-byte. Return a JSON report of created files. (Tools: All tools)
- mason:schema-designer: Delegate to this subagent when the user wants to design a new JSON Schema for an inter-agent artifact — a structured payload passed between producers and consumers in the plugin ecosystem. Provide a description of what the artifact represents, who produces it, and who consumes it. The designer produces a JSON Schema following ecosystem conventions (draft 2020-12, $id as name@version, all fields documented, reasoning scratchpad field always present, additionalProperties false, required fields listed), checks for conflicts with existing schemas in shared/schemas/, and returns the schema object with a recommended filename. (Tools: All tools)
- muse:auditor: Delegate to this subagent when you need adversarial quality review of a component spec@1 before it enters planning. Input is a spec@1 JSON object describing a UI component. Checks for completeness: missing interactive states (hover, focus, active, disabled, loading, error, empty), missing accessibility criteria (role, name, focus order, keyboard operability, live-region or state-announcement behavior), invalid prop combinations not marked as error cases, ambiguous phrasing, scope overlap with other component specs, and unnecessary prose that costs every downstream reader without adding a needed fact. For every issue, produces the rewritten fix, not just a description. Output is a JSON object with an issues array (criterion_id, type, description, suggested_fix) and an overall pass/fail verdict. Standard: can a developer implement this component without one clarifying question? Does not check the spec against source artifacts — that's a verification concern; this checks whether the spec, on its own terms, is complete, unambiguous, and implementable. (Tools: All tools)
- muse:drafter: Delegate to this subagent when you have a completed requirement@1 (or free-text design intent) and need a formal component spec@1 drafted. Input is a requirement@1 and optionally design references (mockup description, existing component family, design-system tokens). Output is a spec@1 conforming to shared/schemas/spec@1.json: id (SPEC-NNN), purpose, scope, non_goals (at least one), acceptance_criteria (at least one), optional api_surface for the component's props. Every criterion must be falsifiable — confirmable by a tester with no implementation knowledge, using only observable behavior: rendered output, focus order, ARIA attributes, emitted events. Props, variants, every interactive state (default, hover, focus, active, disabled, loading, error, empty), and accessibility criteria are each named explicitly. Error cases and invalid prop combinations carry is_error_case: true. Unknowns go in non_goals or reasoning — no TBDs anywhere. The muse orchestrator writes the spec to disk after exit-gate passes; this agent returns the spec object only. Also runs in correction mode: given spec_file_path, a criterion_id, and implementer's contradiction report, revises the affected criterion (and any dependent ones) and returns the full corrected spec@1 with revision_note set. (Tools: All tools)
- muse:exit-gate: Delegate to this subagent when a component spec@1 needs a definitive pass/fail judgment before entering the planning phase. Input is a spec@1 JSON object describing a UI component. This is an adversarial gatekeeper — the default disposition is fail, and the spec must earn a pass. The spec passes only if all four conditions hold: every acceptance criterion is a testable proposition with no vague language, no TBDs remain anywhere in the document, error cases and invalid prop combinations are explicitly covered with is_error_case: true criteria, and every interactive state and accessibility criterion (role, name, focus order, keyboard operability) implied by the component's props is present. On fail, every blocker is specific enough for the drafter to make a targeted fix without further clarification. Output is a verdict@1 conforming to shared/schemas/verdict@1.json with artifact_type set to spec@1. This agent is the binding exit gate — its fail verdict halts progression to navigator until the spec is corrected and resubmitted. Maximum 3 retries before escalation to a human reviewer. (Tools: All tools)
- navigator:challenger: Delegate to this subagent when a plan@1 needs adversarial review before implementation. Input is a plan@1 and its source spec@1. Check missing work, dependency order, prescription, batching, error handling, criterion coverage, and interface siblings against live evidence. Return per-issue repairs and a binding pass or fail verdict. (Tools: All tools)
- navigator:estimator: Delegate to this subagent when a plan@1 exists and you need a rough effort estimate before committing to execution. Input is a plan@1 JSON object. The agent produces a per-task time estimate in minutes, marks each task as parallelizable or sequential, lists blocking dependencies by task ID, and produces a total_minutes sum with explicit assumptions. The implementer is assumed to have full codebase context but no domain knowledge of the feature being built. A task is marked parallelizable only if it has no dependency on any other task in the current plan. All assumptions affecting the estimate are listed explicitly in an assumptions array. Output is a JSON object with total_minutes, a tasks array, and assumptions. (Tools: All tools)
- navigator:planner: Delegate to this subagent when you have a completed spec@1 and need a sequenced, executable implementation plan. Input is a spec@1 (or its spec_file_path, read from disk if provided). Output is a plan@1 conforming to shared/schemas/plan@1.json, with spec_file_path and spec_hash propagated from the spec. Decomposes into dependency-ordered tasks (foundational types, then logic, then integration); each task includes exact file paths, a brief implementation approach, exact implementation code as a concrete baseline (smith's implementer may improve on its shape, not its scope), the exact tests proving each criterion it covers, the verification command, a commit message, and covers_criteria naming every acceptance criterion it addresses. Every criterion must appear in some task's covers_criteria. Each task is one independently reviewable unit of change, sized to its Subsystem Batch's compilation boundary rather than a clock-time estimate; no TBDs. Also runs in amend mode: given an existing plan@1, a corrected spec@1, and the changed criterion_ids, patches only the affected tasks (adding new ones for newly introduced criteria) and leaves the rest untouched. Route output to challenger. (Tools: All tools)
- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- ranger:adversary: Invoke once per candidate after scanner and, for T7 or T10, boundary tracing. Try to refute reachability from current code and return `candidate-assessment@1`. (Tools: All tools)
- ranger:boundary-tracer: Trace T7 and T10 candidates across execution boundaries. Supports Rust, TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, and Go. Return `field-survival-map@1`. (Tools: All tools)
- ranger:exit-gate: Independently verify remediated `finding-report@2` entries and their defect families against current code. Return `verdict@3`. (Tools: All tools)
- ranger:recon: Invoke before scanning. Detect affected languages, trace reachable files from live entry points, and inventory project capabilities and current workspace state. Return `workspace-manifest@1`; do not judge defects. (Tools: All tools)
- ranger:scanner: Invoke after recon. Load the hazard pack for each scoped language, scan only live files, and emit every matching `candidate@1` without verdicting. Supports Rust, TypeScript/JavaScript, Python, and Go. (Tools: All tools)
- scribe:arch-auditor: Delegate to this subagent when a draft spec@1 needs checking against the workspace's whole-system architecture before it enters scribe/gate-spec — not against another spec, and not against a single function's signature, but against module boundaries, canonical abstractions, and invariants that span the codebase. Input is a spec@1 draft plus workspace_root. Default (check) mode: reads the persisted arch-model@2 at docs/architecture/model.json (or notes it is absent), reads broadly enough across the workspace to confirm the model still reflects reality, and checks the spec against it — flagging boundary violations (a dependency running the wrong direction), competing abstractions (a new type reinventing something the model already canonicalizes), and invariant conflicts. Output is an arch-audit@1 conforming to shared/schemas/arch-audit@1.json. Build mode: given no usable model or an explicit refresh request, reads the codebase broadly and produces or updates an arch-model@2 conforming to shared/schemas/arch-model@2.json — module boundaries, canonical abstractions, and invariants (each citing its governing decision record when one exists), the latter cumulative across everything scribe/architect has ever fixed. This agent does not patch specs or code — it reports fit, or builds the model fit is checked against. (Tools: All tools)
- scribe:architect: Delegate when `finding-report@2`, `implementation-review@2`, or `implementation-result@1` identifies a structural defect class. Inspect the live semantic model and persisted architecture, then produce a `spec@1` that makes recurrence impossible or machine-detectable. (Tools: All tools)
- scribe:auditor: Delegate to this subagent when you need adversarial quality review of a spec@1 before it enters planning. Input is a spec@1 JSON object. Checks seven dimensions: untestable/vague criteria, ambiguous phrasing, missing error cases, scope overlap with other specs, TBDs/incomplete sections, unnecessary prose that costs every downstream reader without adding a needed fact, and a field this spec introduces or changes on a type that another spec persists, serializes, or transmits with no matching round-trip criterion on the far side and no note that the gap is intentional. For every issue, produces the rewritten fix, not just a description. Output is a JSON object with an issues array (criterion_id, type, description, suggested_fix) and an overall pass/fail verdict. Standard: can a developer implement this spec without one clarifying question? Does not check the spec against source artifacts — that's verifier's role; this checks whether the spec, on its own terms, is complete, unambiguous, and implementable. (Tools: All tools)
- scribe:drafter: Delegate to this subagent when you have a completed requirement@1 and need a formal spec@1 drafted. Input is a requirement@1 and optionally a research-report@1. Output is a spec@1 conforming to shared/schemas/spec@1.json: id (SPEC-NNN), purpose, scope, non_goals (at least one), acceptance_criteria (at least one), optional api_surface. Every criterion must be falsifiable — confirmable by a tester with no implementation knowledge, using only observable behavior. Error cases carry is_error_case: true. Unknowns go in non_goals or reasoning — no TBDs anywhere. The scribe orchestrator writes the spec to disk after exit-gate passes; this agent returns the spec object only. Also runs in correction mode: given spec_file_path, a criterion_id, and implementer's contradiction report, revises the affected criterion (and any dependent ones) and returns the full corrected spec@1 with revision_note set. (Tools: All tools)
- scribe:drift-checker: On-demand diagnostic: given a spec_file_path and a workspace root, verifies the current code still implements every acceptance criterion in the spec. Reads the spec from disk, not from context, and reads implementation/tests from the workspace. When a prior changeset@2's criteria_evidence is available, uses its pointers as a starting point but re-verifies each one — code may have moved since it was recorded. Classifies each criterion as covered (implementation and tests match the contract), uncovered (nothing found), or drifted (behavior diverges from the criterion). Not a blocking gate — exit-gate is. Use for ongoing maintenance, detecting drift weeks or months after implementation. Output is a drift report with covered/uncovered/drifted arrays plus a summary. (Tools: All tools)
- scribe:exit-gate: Issue the binding `verdict@3` for a `spec@1` before planning. Pass only when every criterion is testable, error behavior is explicit, no TBD remains, scope fits one planning cycle, and all checks are complete. (Tools: All tools)
- scribe:verifier: Delegate to this subagent when you need to verify that a draft spec@1 is grounded in its source artifacts — the requirement@1 and optional research-report@1 — before it proceeds to auditing or gating. Input is a spec@1 draft plus the originating requirement@1 and any research-report@1 used to produce it. For each acceptance criterion, the agent checks whether the requirement or research report supplies evidence that the criterion is necessary and correctly scoped. Each criterion is classified as supported (evidence found with a direct citation), unsupported (criterion appears with no basis in the source artifacts), or overfitted (criterion is narrower than the source supports, excluding valid cases). The agent collects evidence only and does not produce a pass/fail verdict. Output is a structured evidence report with supported, unsupported, and overfitted arrays plus a reasoning scratchpad. For post-implementation drift checking, use drift-checker instead. (Tools: All tools)
- sentinel:exit-gate: Issue `verdict@3` from a completed verification report. Separate blockers, coverage gaps, and pending checks; pass only within the verified scope. (Tools: All tools)
- sentinel:recon: Delegate to this subagent at the start of the sentinel gate protocol when an artifact must be inventoried before verification begins. Input is an artifact path or description. The agent determines the artifact type, locates it in the workspace, enumerates the criteria it must be verified against (derived from a linked spec or requirement, or from the artifact's own acceptance criteria section if none is linked), and identifies source files to cross-check during verification. This is purely mechanical discovery — the agent produces no pass/fail opinion. Output is a JSON manifest with artifact_type, artifact_path, criteria array, source_files array, and a reasoning scratchpad. Do not delegate here for judgment; route the manifest to verifier for criterion cross-reference. (Tools: All tools)
- sentinel:verifier: Delegate to this subagent after recon has produced its artifact manifest, and before any final verdict is issued. Input is the recon manifest from recon, including the artifact path, criteria list, and source files. The agent reads the artifact and each source file and, for each criterion, collects concrete evidence that confirms or refutes it. Each criterion is classified as verified (positive evidence found), failed (evidence contradicts the criterion), or unverifiable (requires external context not accessible). Absence of a counter-example is not sufficient to classify a criterion as verified. This agent is a neutral evidence collector — it does not issue verdicts. Output is a JSON object with verified, failed, and unverifiable arrays. Route output to exit-gate for the final verdict. (Tools: All tools)
- smith:exit-gate: Delegate after all planned batches have terminal results and approved `implementation-review@2` artifacts. Verify current code, scoped evidence, sibling completeness, and pending work independently. Return `verdict@3`. (Tools: All tools)
- smith:implementer: Delegate to execute one plan task. Read persisted criteria, design and implement the change, prove it with tests, and record exact evidence. Commit only when the caller supplies `commit_authorized: true`; otherwise return a null commit SHA. Report spec contradictions or architecture needs instead of forcing a pass. Scope is one task. (Tools: All tools)
- smith:mutator: Delegate after implementation. Use available project-native mutation tooling against changed behavior, or a controlled deliberate fault when appropriate. Analyze survivors and return `mutation-report@2`; unavailable tooling becomes a coverage gap. (Tools: All tools)
- smith:recon: Delegate before implementation. Inspect current workspace state, affected languages, entry points, project-native verification capabilities, baseline tests, and persisted artifact freshness. Return `workspace-manifest@1`; stop on a failing baseline. (Tools: All tools)
- smith:reviewer: Delegate after an implementation batch and discrimination check. Review scope, verification fit, related defects, semantic models, and architecture. Return `implementation-review@2`; route structural families to `scribe:architect`. (Tools: All tools)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)
- vanguard:reader: Delegate to this subagent after recon produces a source map. Input is the source map from recon plus the original research question. The agent reads every identified source and extracts findings relevant to the question, with a citation, confidence level (confirmed, likely, or assumed), and source attribution for each. Does not synthesize or recommend — extracts faithfully from what it reads. Sources that cannot be read are noted as unreadable rather than skipped. Output is a JSON object containing a findings array, a sources_read list, and a reasoning scratchpad noting contradictions or surprises. Do not skip any source from the map; recon already filtered for relevance. Route output to synthesizer. (Tools: All tools)
- vanguard:recon: Delegate to this subagent at the start of any research task, before any reading or analysis begins. Input is a requirement@1 or free-text research question. The agent maps where answers might live — existing specs, docs, manifests, codebase patterns, or external sources — and returns a structured research agenda that tells reader exactly which sources to read. Does not read file contents; relevance is assessed from names and directory structure only. Output is a JSON object containing internal_sources, external_keywords, existing_implementations, scope, and a reasoning scratchpad. The source list is intentionally focused: only sources likely to answer the question, not every file in the workspace. Route output to reader. (Tools: All tools)
- vanguard:risk-assessor: Delegate to this subagent when a proposed approach or research-report@1 needs risk review before a spec is written. Input is a proposed approach or research-report@1 JSON, optionally accompanied by context about the target environment. The agent identifies technical risks that would materially affect the spec or plan if left unaddressed. For each risk it produces a description, severity (critical, high, medium, or low), likelihood, a concrete trigger condition describing when the risk materializes, and a mitigation sketch. Only risks with a plausible failure path are included — theoretical concerns without a realistic trigger are excluded. Output is a JSON object with a prioritized risks array and an overall_risk assessment. Surfaces risks neutrally — no recommendation about whether to proceed. (Tools: All tools)
- vanguard:synthesizer: Delegate to this subagent after reader produces a findings list. Input is the findings array and reasoning from reader, along with the original research question. The agent synthesizes findings into a coherent research-report@1, surfaces contradictions between sources, identifies patterns across findings, and lists open questions that remain unanswered. Output is a complete research-report@1 conforming to shared/schemas/research-report@1.json. The recommendation includes an explicit confidence level (high, medium, or low), the rationale, a list of open questions, and any contradictions called out explicitly. Does not resolve contradictions by choosing a side without evidence — accuracy over tidiness. Route output to scribe. (Tools: All tools)
- weaver:auditor: Delegate to this subagent to cross-reference open requirements against existing specs, persisted plans, and implementation files. Input is a list of open requirement@1 objects. Searches for files that address each requirement's done_when criteria — including a persisted plan@1 at docs/projects/ covering the requirement's linked spec, not just a gated spec or shipped implementation — inspects matches for substance, and detects requirements with overlapping or identical core statements. Output is a structured audit report: per-requirement status (covered, partial, missing, duplicate), evidence, duplicate_of references, and a structured summary (per-status counts plus an optional one-clause note). Read-only — modifies nothing. Use before planning to prevent duplicate work. Also runs in a narrower connect mode: given one requirement@1 (or a small set) instead of the full backlog, returns the same per-requirement shape scoped to just what was given. (Tools: All tools)
- weaver:clarifier: Delegate to this subagent when a requirement@1 draft from intake needs review for missing or underspecified dimensions before a spec can be written. Input is a requirement@1 JSON object. The agent evaluates gaps in priority order: testability of done_when criteria, specificity of stakeholder, and explicitness of out_of_scope boundaries. It then either asks one focused clarifying question or, if all dimensions are complete, returns the finished requirement with out_of_scope fully populated. Never asks multiple questions at once — one question per invocation. Output is a JSON object with action (question or complete), question (or null), the current requirement, and reasoning. When action is complete, out_of_scope is populated with explicit scope boundaries. Route completed requirements to drafter. (Tools: All tools)
- weaver:intake: Delegate to this subagent when you have a raw need statement in free text — a problem description, user story, or feature request — and need it converted into a structured requirement@1 draft. Input is unstructured text only; no schema is required from the caller. The agent infers id, statement, stakeholder, why, and done_when from the provided text without asking any clarifying questions. Fields that cannot be inferred are omitted; gaps are noted in the reasoning scratchpad. The out_of_scope field is intentionally left empty — populating it is the clarifier's responsibility. Output is a flat requirement@1 JSON object conforming to shared/schemas/requirement@1.json. Every done_when criterion must be a testable proposition verifiable from outside the implementation. Route this output directly to clarifier before writing a spec. (Tools: All tools)
- weaver:prioritizer: Delegate to this subagent when a set of requirement@1 drafts needs ranking before planning starts. Input is a list of requirement@1 objects. The agent ranks them by impact (who is affected and how badly), urgency (signals in why/done_when indicating time pressure), and dependency order (a requirement that another depends on ranks above the one depending on it, regardless of its own impact/urgency score). Output is an ordered list with a stated rationale per requirement, plus any dependency relationships found. Does not modify requirement@1 objects — ranking and rationale only. (Tools: All tools)

When you launch multiple agents for independent work, send them in a single message with multiple tool uses so they run concurrently.

# MCP Server Instructions

The following MCP servers have provided instructions for how to use their tools and resources:

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>\n\n<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>\n\n<?claude block s1?>\n\n<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

17	### [Critical→fixed] `status`/`plan-publish`/`validate` all crashed on the wasm path — `tags.rs` had no CommandRunner fallback
18	- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04 (`just ci` green, real end-to-end wasm sandbox regression test)
19	- **Location**: `crates/callisto-graph/src/tags.rs` (`last_tag_for`, `TagIndex::build`)

21	- **Root Cause**: `last_tag_for` took an unused `_runner: &R` (`CommandRunner`) parameter and unconditionally called `callisto_vcs::GitRepository::discover(root)?` (gix, native-only). On `wasm32`, `discover` always returns `Err`, so this propagated straight up through `TagIndex::build` and killed `Workspace::load` on the very first package for any real moon invocation — before any actual git logic ran. Found by direct re-reading of `tags.rs`/`changed.rs` after the architecture discussion concluded gix must stay native-only; `changed.rs` already had the correct gix-try/`CommandRunner`-fallback shape, `tags.rs` never did.

Glob-matching against the raw tag list now happens in `callisto-graph` itself (mirroring `callisto-vcs`'s `globset` semantics exactly), so tag selection is byte-identical regardless of which path sourced the list. `TagIndex::build` now fetches the tag list once and reuses it across all packages (was: once per package) — fixes both the wasm32 crash and the O(N) host-round-trip performance gap flagged in the architecture discussion.
23	- **Verification**: reproduced the crash pre-fix through the real compiled `.wasm` under a real wasmtime sandbox (`exit_code: 1`, `E_GRAPH`, "gix native git operations disabled on WASM target"), confirmed `exit_code: 0` with the correct `lastTag` post-fix — genuine end-to-end evidence, not just a unit test. # Bug-Hunter Findings Ledger

Append-only log of findings from prior bug-hunter runs. Check this before starting a new sweep so you don't re-spend budget rediscovering the same bug. Update an entry's `Fix Status` in place when it changes — don't delete history, mark it.

Format: one entry per confirmed finding. `Fix Status: unfixed | fix applied, untested | fixed (test run + date)`.

---

### [Medium] PEP 735 Dependency Groups declared supported in spec, entirely unimplemented in code
- **Status**: CONFIRMED (2026-08-03 sweep)
- **Location**: `crates/callisto-manifests/src/python.rs:183-256` (`iter_dependencies`), `:258-343` (`update_dependency_spec`); spec: `docs/04-python-engine-spec.md:14`
- **Classification**: Spec Drift
- **Root Cause**: The Python engine spec lists PEP 735 (`[dependency-groups]`) as one of 5 core PEPs supported. `python.rs` only reads/writes `[project].dependencies` and `[tool.poetry.dependencies]` — no code anywhere references `dependency-groups`.
- **Failing Scenario**: A `pyproject.toml` with `[dependency-groups] test = ["pytest>=7.0"]` pinning an in-workspace sibling — a cascade-triggering bump never rewrites the entry, invisible to cascade/validate/version alike.
- **Fix Status**: unfixed — spec-correction/spec-completion pass dispatched 2026-08-03, code fix not yet started, pending that pass landing.

### [Critical→fixed] `status`/`plan-publish`/`validate` all crashed on the wasm path — `tags.rs` had no CommandRunner fallback
- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04 (`just ci` green, real end-to-end wasm sandbox regression test)
- **Location**: `crates/callisto-graph/src/tags.rs` (`last_tag_for`, `TagIndex::build`)
- **Classification**: Discarded Parameter / Architecture Gap
- **Root Cause**: `last_tag_for` took an unused `_runner: &R` (`CommandRunner`) parameter and unconditionally called `callisto_vcs::GitRepository::discover(root)?` (gix, native-only). On `wasm32`, `discover` always returns `Err`, so this propagated straight up through `TagIndex::build` and killed `Workspace::load` on the very first package for any real moon invocation — before any actual git logic ran. Found by direct re-reading of `tags.rs`/`changed.rs` after the architecture discussion concluded gix must stay native-only; `changed.rs` already had the correct gix-try/`CommandRunner`-fallback shape, `tags.rs` never did.
- **Fix**: `fetch_all_tags` (new) tries gix first, falls through (not `?`) to one `runner.run("git", &["tag","--list"], root)` call when unavailable — mirroring `changed.rs`'s existing pattern exactly, so no new design was invented. Glob-matching against the raw tag list now happens in `callisto-graph` itself (mirroring `callisto-vcs`'s `globset` semantics exactly), so tag selection is byte-identical regardless of which path sourced the list. `TagIndex::build` now fetches the tag list once and reuses it across all packages (was: once per package) — fixes both the wasm32 crash and the O(N) host-round-trip performance gap flagged in the architecture discussion.
- **Verification**: reproduced the crash pre-fix through the real compiled `.wasm` under a real wasmtime sandbox (`exit_code: 1`, `E_GRAPH`, "gix native git operations disabled on WASM target"), confirmed `exit_code: 0` with the correct `lastTag` post-fix — genuine end-to-end evidence, not just a unit test. Also added a call-counting test proving the N→1 batching.
- **Fix Status**: fixed.

### [Medium→fixed] `Version::deserialize` was hardcoded to `VersionGrammar::SemVer`, silently broken for PEP-440-only strings
- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04 — the earlier deferral was revisited with real investigation, not just implemented blind
- **Location**: `crates/callisto-model/src/version.rs`
- **Classification**: Spec Drift
- **Investigation**: grepped every real serde-deserialization call site for a `Version`-bearing type; found exactly one with no available grammar signal — `commands/tag.rs`'s `PublishPlan` ingestion (reads a plan file/stdin from a potentially separate process/CI step, no sibling ecosystem field). Confirmed no PEP-440 `Version` reaches that path *today* (`plan_publish` has no `PublishTarget::Pypi` branch yet), but PyPI/PEP 440 is a fully live, non-stub ecosystem elsewhere in the codebase (manifest parsing, bump logic, and the publish-client classifier are all already implemented) — so this was going to silently break the moment that wiring gap closed.
- **Fix**: `Version::deserialize` now tries `SemVer` first (strictest/most unambiguous), falls back to `Pep440` only if that fails — mirroring `VersionReq::deserialize`'s existing multi-grammar pattern. Residual ambiguity (a string valid under both grammars always resolves to SemVer) is documented directly on the impl and pinned by a test, matching the same accepted tradeoff `VersionReq` already carries.
- **Fix Status**: fixed.

### [High→fixed] `callisto-moon`'s exec seam didn't route a missing-binary host-abort through its own promised `Result` — affected both `execute_extension` and `initialize_extension`
- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04
- **Location**: `crates/callisto-moon/src/runner.rs`
- **Classification**: Silent Fallback / Crash-Safety (falsifies the crate's own "never panics, every failure caught into the report" claim)
- **Root Cause**: When the target program (`moon`/`git`) can't be resolved, `warpgate` 0.30.5's host-side `exec_command` closure returns `Err` from *native* code — Extism aborts the entire plugin call rather than routing it back into the guest as a value the guest's own `Result` handling can see. `MoonCommandRunner::run`'s `Err(e) => classify_host_failure(...)` branch never ran; the whole host call failed instead.
- **Fix**: Pre-check existence via `warpgate_pdk::command_exists` (shells to `which`, not the target program, so a missing program yields an ordinary `false`) before calling `exec`, turning it into the clean `CommandError::NotFound` the method already promised.
- **Fix Status**: fixed. Found only because the new black-box failure-path tests (dispatched to close a coverage gap) immediately falsified the "never panics" claim on first write — exactly the kind of bug happy-path-only testing had been hiding.

### [Medium] Per-package git-repo discovery + revwalk in severity inference — O(N_packages × C_commits) instead of O(C_commits)
- **Status**: CONFIRMED (2026-08-04, performance sweep)
- **Location**: `crates/callisto-graph/src/aggregate.rs:183-228`, `crates/callisto-graph/src/infer.rs:53-74`, `crates/callisto-conventional/src/window.rs:22-31`
- **Classification**: Architectural / Algorithmic complexity
- **Root Cause**: `aggregate()` reuses a single `GitRepository` for `resolve_since`, but severity inference is separate — for every package, `fetch_commits` re-discovers the repo and runs its own independent revwalk + tree-diff from HEAD to that package's `since` bound. Most packages share largely the same commit window, so the tree-diff work over the shared range repeats once per package instead of once total.
- **Failing Scenario**: 150-package monorepo, most untagged in the last 40 commits — `aggregate()` triggers 150 separate `gix::discover` calls and 150 independent tree-diff walks over an overlapping range, instead of one HEAD walk bucketing each commit's touched paths against all pathspecs at once.
- **Fix Status**: unfixed, not yet dispatched. Note: with the `GitDataSource`/`GitAccess` abstraction now in place (see below), `resolve_since` and `fetch_commits` both go through a shared, single-discovery `GitAccess` instance per `aggregate()` call already — this finding is specifically about the per-package *revwalk/tree-diff* work still repeating, not repo re-discovery (that part is already fixed as a byproduct of the trait consolidation).

### [Architecture] Formalized the recurring gix-vs-CommandRunner fallback pattern into a real `GitDataSource` trait
- **Status**: Landed 2026-08-04 — not a bug fix, a consolidation. Logged here since it directly addresses the root cause behind 5 separate bugs found and fixed earlier this session (`tags.rs`, `commands/tag.rs`, `aggregate.rs`, `window.rs`, plus `changed.rs`'s pre-existing correct instance).
- **Location**: new `crates/callisto-vcs/src/{shell.rs, access.rs}`, trait in `crates/callisto-vcs/src/lib.rs`
- **Design**: `GitDataSource` trait (`list_tags`/`resolve_commit`/`commits_since`/`create_tag`/`create_floating_major`) with two implementers — `GitRepository` (existing native/gix) and new `ShellGit` (the `CommandRunner`-shelled backend, consolidated from the five hand-rolled duplicates). New `GitAccess` is the selection layer: `GitAccess::discover(root, runner)` tries gix once, applies **asymmetric fallback policy** — reads retry through the shell on any native error, but write ops (`create_tag`/`create_floating_major`) are authoritative once gix is discovered and never masked by a shell retry, preserving the exact invariant `commands/tag.rs`'s original fix established. All five call sites migrated; ~200 lines of duplicated fallback logic removed (e.g. `aggregate.rs`'s `resolve_since` went from a 25-line hand-rolled fallback to a one-line trait call).
- **Bundled fix**: `commits_since`'s unbounded-full-history-walk-on-unresolvable-ref bug (previously its own ledger entry) is fixed as part of this consolidation — an unresolved `since_ref` now returns `Err(VcsError::RefNotFound)` in both backends instead of silently walking everything.
- **Verified**: `cargo test --workspace` 324/324, plus 15 new tests for the trait/backends themselves (glob rejection, native-vs-shell routing, write-op non-retry, `RefNotFound` propagation).

### [Critical→fixed] `callisto-moon`'s exec seam is a native-process stub — gix-in-WASM spike ruled out as a fix, host-exec bridge landed
- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04 (`just ci` green, including real black-box `.wasm` sandbox tests)
- **Location**: `crates/callisto-moon/src/runner.rs`
- **Classification**: Crash-Safety / Architecture Gap
- **Root Cause**: Implemented `CommandRunner` via `std::process::Command::new(program).output()`, which cannot function under WASI sandboxing (WASM guests can't spawn processes). A dedicated spike investigated whether gitoxide's low-level crates could instead read the repo natively from inside the guest (moon does grant a real WASI preopen at `/workspace`) — **NO-GO**: `gix-odb`/`gix-pack`/`gix-index` all read object/index content via `memmap2::Mmap` unconditionally; `memmap2` has no `wasm32-wasip1` backend and its stub returns `io::ErrorKind::Unsupported` at runtime. Ref *names* resolve (loose refs use plain `std::fs`), but no object content is readable — confirmed via a real wasmtime run against a real fixture repo, not just static analysis.
- **Fix**: `MoonCommandRunner` now bridges through `warpgate_pdk::exec` (the real `#[host_fn] exec_command` binding) on the `pdk` (wasm) build, keeping the original `std::process::Command` path only for native (non-wasm) builds. Verified with genuine black-box coverage: `crates/callisto-moon/tests/moon_wasm_sandbox.rs` builds the actual `.wasm`, loads it into a real wasmtime-backed Extism sandbox via `moon_pdk_test_utils`, and drives real `register_extension`/`execute_extension` wire calls — not just a type-check.
- **Follow-on bug found and fixed during final verification**: the fix's `Cargo.toml` initially declared `crate-type = ["cdylib", "rlib"]` unconditionally, which made `cargo llvm-cov --all-features` (native, macOS) also attempt a **native** cdylib build/link whenever the `pdk` feature was on, failing on extism-pdk's WASM-host-only import symbols (`_alloc`, `_input_length`, etc. — undefined for native linking). Fixed by removing `crate-type` from the manifest entirely and instead requesting `--crate-type cdylib` explicitly only where the wasm artifact is actually needed (`just wasm-check`, the test's self-bootstrap build) via `cargo rustc --crate-type cdylib`.
- **Also found and fixed during final verification**: `moon_pdk_test_utils`'s test-only dependency chain (`warpgate` → `extism` host crate → `wasmtime 41.0.4`) carries several open RUSTSEC advisories (sandbox-escape/miscompile class) plus one unmaintained-crate warning, none of which ship in the production `.wasm` artifact (only the lightweight guest-side `warpgate_pdk` does, which is unaffected). Scoped, documented `[advisories] ignore` added to `deny.toml` for these specific IDs — flagged there as **unstable across consecutive runs** (the RustSec advisory-db itself appears to be actively updated mid-session), so this list may need to grow again on a future CI run.
- **Fix Status**: fixed.

## Fixed — 2026-08-04 batch (PEP 440, native git-on-gix unification, moon protocol types, publish orchestrator)

- **PEP 440 post+dev combined bump produced a version lower than the input** — `bump.rs`'s `finalize_in_place` condition only checked `is_dev()`, never `is_post()`; a version like `1.2.3.post1.dev1` (which PEP 440 ranks above `1.2.3`) incorrectly finalized to `1.2.3` on a Patch bump. Fixed to only finalize-in-place when there's no post segment.
- **PEP 440 non-canonical input broke `Eq`/`Hash`** — `Version` stored the caller's literal `raw` string instead of canonical form; `1.0.0-alpha1` and `1.0.0a1` compared equal via `.compare()` but not via `==`/`Hash`. Fixed by normalizing `raw` to `pep440_rs`'s canonical rendering on parse.
- **Git-access inconsistency (gix vs. shelling to the `git` binary)** — `aggregate.rs`'s tag-to-SHA resolution and `callisto-conventional`'s pathspec-scoped commit log both shelled to `git` via `CommandRunner`, inconsistent with `callisto-vcs`'s native `gix` usage everywhere else. Both now go through new `GitRepository::resolve_commit`/`commits_since_with_pathspec` methods — no git-binary shelling left in the native (non-WASM) codebase.
- **`callisto-moon` protocol type mismatches (Register/Execute/Initialize)** — see the entries below for what's now fixed vs. still open on the moon front.

## Fixed — Batch 2 hardening (landed and verified 2026-08-03, `just ci` green, 178/178 tests)

- **Linked-group version convergence** and **pre-release pinned baseline** (`cascade.rs`) — both fixed together; linked members now converge to a single winning target version via `Version::compare`, and pre-release bumps now use `pre.initial_versions` as the pinned base instead of the on-disk value.
- **PackageId cross-ecosystem match ambiguity** — `PackageId::matches()` itself left as correct pairwise semantics; the real fix is a new `resolve_target_package()` in `aggregate.rs` used at the one dangerous call site (changeset-to-package resolution), returning `GraphError::AmbiguousName` instead of silently picking a package when a bare name matches two ecosystems.
- **CST fidelity**: `CargoToml::open` now strips BOM (defense-in-depth; `toml_edit` 0.22.27 already handled it internally); `PyprojectToml` now fingerprints and restores BOM/CRLF on write, mirroring npm.rs; `write_dependency`'s inline-table/full-table branches now clone/reapply decor.
- **Changelog crash-safety**: local `atomic_write` in `callisto-changelog/src/write.rs` replaced with the canonical `callisto_manifests::atomic::atomic_write`.
- **4x redundant manifest reads** — now cached across the three read-only open sites (discovery/`publish_targets`/`iter_dependencies`/`base_versions`); the write-open path was deliberately left uncached per the scoped design.
- **npm dirty in-memory state on error** — `update_dependency_spec` no longer mutates `overrides`/`resolutions` before validating the target exists.

---

## Fixed (re-verified 2026-08-03 against current HEAD, no action needed)

- **Stale dependency-version rewrite on re-cascade** (`cascade.rs`) — `out.rewrites.entry(key).or_insert(...)` replaced with `out.rewrites.insert(...)` (overwrite); re-escalated packages now correctly overwrite dependents' rewrite entries when the fixpoint drains.
- **`compose-pr-body` near-empty output** (`aggregate.rs`, `pr_body.rs`) — `inference.infer(...)` is now actually called and folded in; `PrBodyOptions` (`existing_body`/`labels`/`branch`) is now read.
- **`validate.rs` no-op** — loaded changesets now produce real `EmptyChangeset`/`UnknownPackage` diagnostics; `is_valid` is derived from diagnostic severity, not hardcoded.
- **`plan-publish` proxy signal** — now runs the real `plan_version` pipeline first; tag-vs-manifest diff is only a fallback for packages absent from the bump plan.
- **`--dry-run` never checked** — `transient: global.dry_run` is wired through to `ApplyOptions`; `apply.rs` gates all writes on `!opts.transient`.
- **Miette diagnostics dead code** — `main.rs` now prints `miette::Report::new(err)` via `Debug`, which invokes miette's fancy renderer (this is correct, not a plain `Display` dump).

---

## Known-unverified external claims — resolved

- ~~"Silent fallback version defaults" (`cascade.rs:278-297` `unwrap_or_else`)~~ — RESOLVED, stale claim. That code path no longer exists; `bump_target` now uses `ok_or_else` returning a proper `GraphError`, no silent default.
- "Pre-release lifecycle verified in `lifecycle_e2e_tests.rs`" — superseded by the new pinned-`initial_versions` finding above; the claimed verification did not catch this.
- "Dependency range/catalog constraint calculation verified" — still not independently re-checked.

23	- Pre-release npm packages (`2.0.0-beta.1`) get no `--tag next`. They land on `latest` and break every consumer pinned to stable.

29	
30	**Fix**: Call `client.load_plan(&plan)` in `cli/commands/publish.rs` before constructing the orchestrator. Add an integration test that goes `plan -> load_plan -> RegistryClient::publish -> captured argv`.

35	**File**: `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/publish_client.rs:326`

39	From a clean checkout or CI runner, `dist/` does not exist. twine exits non-zero with `InvalidDistribution: Cannot find file (or expand pattern)`. This is classified as `RegistryError::Other` — 100% failure rate on fresh environments.

50	After `callisto version` bumps `Cargo.toml` versions, `Cargo.lock` becomes stale. `apply.rs:205-222` stages the **stale** `Cargo.lock` into the release commit. On the next run, `cargo publish --locked` aborts: "the lock file needs to be updated but --locked was passed."

52	**This repo's own CI accidentally masks it**: `setup-callisto/action.yml:67-70` runs `cargo build -p callisto-cli` in the release job, which rewrites `Cargo.lock` before `callisto publish` runs. 54	`ApplyOutcome::lockfile_refresh_results` is permanently `None`. `VersionReport.lockfileRefreshResults` is a dead schema field.

61	**File**: `crates/callisto-graph/src/walk.rs:90`

64	- `npm_platform_packages` in every publish plan is always `[]`
65	- `depends_on_platforms` in every `NpmMainPublish` is always `[]`
66	- The entire `napi.rs` module (`NapiTargetsIndex`, `triple_to_role`, `role_to_triple`, `napi_drift`) has zero effective call sites

96	Any genuine failure (auth, verify, manifest error) whose output happens to contain the digits "429" is classified as `RegistryError::RateLimited(60s)` and handed to the **unbounded** retry loop at `publish.rs:354-377`, which has no attempt counter. 155	**File**: `crates/callisto-cli/src/commands/publish.rs:64`

- npm `access` field is never set (see P0-AUTH-001).

The unit tests that claim to verify metadata threading call the private methods `npm_publish`/`cargo_publish`/`pypi_publish` directly, bypassing `RegistryClient::publish` entirely — structurally incapable of catching this regression.

**Fix**: Call `client.load_plan(&plan)` in `cli/commands/publish.rs` before constructing the orchestrator. Add an integration test that goes `plan -> load_plan -> RegistryClient::publish -> captured argv`.

---

### B1: PyPI publishing is non-functional — `python -m build` never run
**File**: `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/publish_client.rs:326`

`pypi_publish` goes straight to `twine upload --skip-existing dist/<name>-<ver>*`. There is no preceding build step anywhere in the pipeline. `docs/04-python-engine-spec.md §8.3` explicitly mandates the two-step sequence.

From a clean checkout or CI runner, `dist/` does not exist. twine exits non-zero with `InvalidDistribution: Cannot find file (or expand pattern)`. This is classified as `RegistryError::Other` — 100% failure rate on fresh environments.

**Fix**: Run `python -m build --outdir <pkg_path>/dist/` before calling twine. Make the build tool configurable (hatchling, poetry build, etc.) via callisto.toml or pyproject.toml `[tool.callisto]` section.

---

### NEW: `--refresh-lockfiles` is a silent no-op while `--locked` is always passed
**File**: `crates/callisto-graph/src/apply.rs:49` + `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/publish_client.rs:145`

`apply.rs:49` takes `_opts: &ApplyOptions` — completely unused. The CLI advertises `--refresh-lockfiles` as "Regenerate lockfiles after applying the version bumps" but the parameter is never consulted. Meanwhile, `cargo publish` is always invoked with `--locked`.

After `callisto version` bumps `Cargo.toml` versions, `Cargo.lock` becomes stale. `apply.rs:205-222` stages the **stale** `Cargo.lock` into the release commit. On the next run, `cargo publish --locked` aborts: "the lock file needs to be updated but --locked was passed."

**This repo's own CI accidentally masks it**: `setup-callisto/action.yml:67-70` runs `cargo build -p callisto-cli` in the release job, which rewrites `Cargo.lock` before `callisto publish` runs. Any consumer using the prebuilt binary download path (`action.yml:71-73`) gets no such build and hits **100% cargo publish failure**.

`ApplyOutcome::lockfile_refresh_results` is permanently `None`. `VersionReport.lockfileRefreshResults` is a dead schema field.

**Fix**: Implement `--refresh-lockfiles` in `apply.rs` (run `cargo update --workspace` after version bumps, or at minimum `cargo metadata --locked` to validate). Document the prebuilt binary limitation. Remove `--locked` from cargo publish or make it conditional.

---

### F-01 / A1: `ManifestRole::Platform` never assigned — napi.rs is dead code
**File**: `crates/callisto-graph/src/walk.rs:90`

`walk.rs:90` unconditionally creates every `ManifestDecl` with `ManifestRole::Canonical`. No code path ever calls `ManifestDecl::new(..., ManifestRole::Platform, ...)`. Consequently:
- `npm_platform_packages` in every publish plan is always `[]`
- `depends_on_platforms` in every `NpmMainPublish` is always `[]`
- The entire `napi.rs` module (`NapiTargetsIndex`, `triple_to_role`, `role_to_triple`, `napi_drift`) has zero effective call sites
- These symbols are re-exported from the crate root as if they were working public API

**Nuance the investigators missed**: publish ORDER is still correct, because `npm.rs:236` maps `optionalDependencies` to `DepKind::Optional` and `toposort.rs:35` includes `Optional` edges. Platform packages sort before their main package inside `npm_main_packages`. But the plan's platform/main split is permanently dead in the public JSON schema.

**Fix**: Wire `triple_to_role` into the walk path to detect platform packages by name convention or napi triple. Or document the split as unimplemented and remove the dead fields from the schema.

---

### AUTH-001: npm auth never wired in the shipped release workflow
**File**: `.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml:70`

`callisto-release.yml` sets `NPM_TOKEN` as a job env var but never calls `npm config set //registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken $NPM_TOKEN`. npm does not read `NPM_TOKEN` directly; it reads auth exclusively from `.npmrc`. Every npm publish attempt fails with `ENEEDAUTH`.

`docs/06-publishing.md:17` labels Pattern A as "what callisto-action uses" — which is flatly untrue. Users copying either the workflow or the doc get a broken pipeline.

**Fix**: Add `- run: npm config set //registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken $NPM_TOKEN` step before the callisto-action step, or use `actions/setup-node` with `registry-url` set.

---

## P1 — Real Bugs, Significant Impact

### NEW: `detect_rate_limit` matches bare "429" in cargo's own compressed-size output
**File**: `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/publish_client.rs:441`

`detect_rate_limit` does `text_lower.contains("429")` against `stdout + stderr`. `cargo publish` routinely prints:
```
Packaged 42 files, 1.4MiB (429.1KiB compressed)
```

Any genuine failure (auth, verify, manifest error) whose output happens to contain the digits "429" is classified as `RegistryError::RateLimited(60s)` and handed to the **unbounded** retry loop at `publish.rs:354-377`, which has no attempt counter. The job sleeps 60s and re-runs cargo publish forever.

`detect_rate_limit` also runs BEFORE `detect_auth_failure`, so a real 401 whose output contains "429" loops forever instead of failing fast. Same class of false positive: "401"/"403" substring matching in `detect_auth_failure` can fire on compressed-size numbers.

**Fix**: Match HTTP status codes only in context — look for `rate limit` or `Retry-After` header text, or the npm-specific `ERATE_LIMIT`. Don't match bare digits.

---

### F-002 / PUB-002: Unbounded retry loop on rate limiting
**File**: `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/publish.rs:354`

`publish_with_retry` is a bare `loop` with no attempt counter and no cumulative deadline. The 600s ceiling is per-retry, not total. A registry returning `Retry-After: 599s` consistently makes the job loop indefinitely. `AlwaysRetryPolicy::check_rate_limit` unconditionally returns `Ok(())` — its doc comment falsely claims the 600s cutoff bounds total wait.

**Fix**: Add `max_attempts: u32` to `RetryPolicy` and a cumulative wall-clock deadline. Default `AlwaysRetryPolicy` to 3 attempts or 30 minutes total.

---

### F-001 (bun): Bun publish targets workspace root instead of the requested package
**File**: `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/publish_client.rs:241`

The bun branch emits bare `["publish"]` with no package selector and no `cwd` change. Every other package manager targets the package explicitly (`pnpm --filter X`, `yarn workspace X`, `npm --workspace X`). In a bun monorepo, this either publishes the root `package.json` or errors on a private root.

The test at line 1361 only asserts `program == "bun"` — structurally incapable of catching this.

Also: `bun.lock` (text format, bun >= 1.1.1) is not detected — only `bun.lockb` (legacy binary). Modern bun workspaces fall through to the npm branch.

**Fix**: Bun publish must be invoked from the package's own directory (no `--filter` equivalent for bun publish). Add `bun.lock` detection.

---

### NEW: Planned version vs. on-disk version mismatch
**File**: `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/publish.rs:52-57`

`plan_publish` takes `bump.to` (the not-yet-written target version) as the version in the plan, while `cargo publish`/`npm publish` upload whatever the manifest says on disk. Nothing in the publish path writes manifests.

If `callisto publish` is run while changesets are still pending (no guard exists), the tool:
1. Probes `npm view X@<new-version>` — gets not-published
2. Uploads `<old-version>` to the registry
3. Records `PublishAttempt { version: <new-version>, result: Published }`
4. The action then creates a git tag for a version that was never uploaded

The action's `hasChangesets` gate hides this in the happy path. A direct `callisto publish` invocation does not.

**Fix**: Add a pre-publish assertion that the on-disk version of each package matches the planned version. Fail early with an actionable message if not.

---

### AUTH-002: `TWINE_API_TOKEN` documented but does not exist
**File**: `docs/06-publishing.md:117`

The doc states "Twine reads `TWINE_USERNAME` and `TWINE_PASSWORD` (or `TWINE_API_TOKEN`) directly from the environment." `TWINE_API_TOKEN` is not a twine environment variable. Users who set it get a credentials prompt or 403 with no explanation.

`docs/04-python-engine-spec.md §8.4` contradicts `06-publishing.md` and gets this right (`TWINE_USERNAME=__token__` + `TWINE_PASSWORD=pypi-<token>`).

**Fix**: Remove `TWINE_API_TOKEN` reference from `06-publishing.md`. Standardize on `TWINE_USERNAME=__token__` + `TWINE_PASSWORD`.

---

### AUTH-003: No pre-flight credential check
**File**: `crates/callisto-cli/src/commands/publish.rs:64`

No credential presence check before publish begins. Auth failures discovered reactively after partial publishes. In a Cargo+npm repo: Cargo publishes land immutably on crates.io, then npm fails with ENEEDAUTH. Re-running is idempotent (AlreadyPublished = success) but wasted time and a red CI run that misleads the team.

**Fix**: Pre-flight check: verify `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN` (or `~/.cargo/credentials`) is set before any Cargo publish; check npm auth state with `npm whoami` or `.npmrc` inspection; check `TWINE_USERNAME`/`TWINE_PASSWORD` before PyPI.

---

### A2 / F-005: Scoped npm packages default to restricted access
**File**: `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/publish.rs:127`

`access: None` is hardcoded for all npm packages. npm's ecosystem default for `@scoped/packages` is `restricted`. Publishing a scoped package to the public npm registry triggers `402 Payment Required` unless the org has a paid plan.

There is no CLI, callisto.toml, or package.json callisto-field surface to set `access: public`. The comment at `publish.rs:122-126` says callers should set it "before passing the plan to load_plan" — but `load_plan` is never called (PUB-001) and there is no CLI surface.

Note: `publishConfig.access = "public"` in `package.json` works as a workaround since npm reads it directly. But callisto gives no guidance on this.

**Fix**: Detect scoped packages (`name.starts_with('@')`) and default to `NpmAccess::Public` for them. Document `publishConfig.access` as the override mechanism.

---

### F-003: No timeout on subprocess invocations
**File**: `crates/callisto-cli/src/runner.rs:10`

`CliCommandRunner::run` uses `.output()` with no timeout. The `CommandRunner` trait has no timeout parameter. A network stall, hung `cargo publish`, or npm waiting on a tarball upload blocks the callisto process indefinitely.

**Fix**: Wrap in a timeout thread or use `tokio::process` with a deadline. Default 10 minutes per package. Surface as configurable via env var or global arg.

---

### B2 / F-03: twine dist/ path relative to workspace root, not package dir
**File**: `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/publish_client.rs:326`

`pypi_publish` constructs `dist/<normalized>-<version>*` and runs twine from `self.cwd` (workspace root). In a monorepo, build artifacts land at `<pkg>/dist/`, not `<root>/dist/`. The glob matches nothing for every package not at the workspace root.

`SubprocessRegistryClient` has a single `cwd` field with no per-package override — structural fix required.

**Fix**: Add `package_path: PathBuf` to `PypiPublish` in the plan. Use the package's own directory as cwd for twine (and for the build step in B1).

---

### PUB-003: `--dry-run` output never lists packages
**File**: `crates/callisto-cli/src/render/mod.rs:56`

`render_publish` (called by `write_dry_run_text`) correctly counts packages for the empty-plan check, but the non-zero branch only iterates `report.releases` (git tag entries). It never renders any `rust_crates`, `npm_platform_packages`, `npm_main_packages`, or `pypi_packages`. A user running `--dry-run` sees only tag lines — no packages, no versions, no registries.

On a non-git checkout, `releases` is empty and `--dry-run` prints one header line while the plan is non-empty.

**Fix**: Render all four package lists in `write_dry_run_text`. Show: ecosystem, package name, version, registry/tag.

---

### F-006: Private npm registry "already published" not recognized
**File**: `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/publish_client.rs:492`

`classify_npm_publish_output` only recognizes `epublishconflict`, `previously published`, and `cannot publish over`. Private npm-compatible registries (Verdaccio, GitHub Packages, Artifactory) may return `409` with different bodies. Such responses fall through to `RegistryError::Other`, marking the package `Failed` and breaking idempotent re-runs.

**Fix**: Also match HTTP 409 / `e409` in the conflict branch.

---

### NEW: `npm view` exit-0 with empty stdout blocks publish
**File**: `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/publish_client.rs:160`

`npm_is_published` success-with-output returns `true`; a fixed list of E404/etarget strings returns `false`; everything else returns `Err(RegistryError::Other("npm view failed ambiguously (exit Some(0))"))`. npm exits 0 with empty stdout in several valid no-match situations. That error propagates through `is_published()?` at `publish.rs:350` and marks the package `Failed` without ever attempting a publish — a package that is simply not yet published can be permanently unpublishable.

**Fix**: Treat exit-0-with-empty-stdout as `Ok(false)` (not published).

---

## P2 — Real but Lower Blast Radius

|---|---|---|
| F-04 | `publish.rs:118,155` | `NpmPublish::registry` always `None`; `--registry` never passed for npm |
| F-05 | `python.rs:381` | `PypiPublish::index` always `None`; can't target private PyPI |
| F-07 | `python.rs` | `is_publishable` always `true`; no way to mark Python package private |
| F-08 | `publish.rs:182` | "pypi" registry key is a bare string literal, not a constant like `CRATES_IO` |
| F-002 contrib | `publish_client.rs:145` | Cargo private-registry crate: callisto can't publish it (cargo rejects gracefully, but callisto gives no useful error) |
| AUTH-005 | `publish_client.rs:152` | `npm_is_published` always queries public registry; private registry packages always appear unpublished |
| AUTH-006 | `.github/workflows:58` | `id-token: write` granted with no OIDC flow implemented; unused but broadens blast radius |

| PUB-007 | `publish.rs:329` | All `RegistryError` variants collapse to `Failed { error: string }` in JSON |

| ID | File | Issue |
|---|---|---|
| F-06 | `publish.rs:30` | `.ok()` on `plan_version` failure — changeset errors silently swallowed |
| PUB-004 | `commands/publish.rs:66` | Empty real-publish plan shows only a header line, no "nothing to publish" message |

## False Alarm

**A4**: Demand for compensating transaction when main package publish fails after platform packages succeed. npm and crates.io have no rollback primitive. Re-running is already idempotent via `AlreadyPublished`. Not implementable, not needed.

---

## Fix Priority Order

# Entire repository agent guide — Brain

Use Brain for task context and retained knowledge. Begin substantive tasks needing
orientation with:

    entire brain brief "<task>" --json

Run it before deciding the task does not need it: what the brief adds is the part
you do not already know about.

Questions about why something is the way it is, what was decided, or what was
tried before are answered by durable memories. Retrieve them directly; the brief's
memories section is a sample, not the search:

    entire brain recall "<question>" --json

recall ranks decisions, rejected approaches, invariants and gotchas first. query
mixes memories with history and documentation and can rank documentation above the
recorded decision.

Reuse useful code locations from the brief. Use Brain retrieval for previous
decisions, attempts, documentation, and durable memories - Brain's episodic record
of what was decided, what went wrong before, and what must stay true. Record one
when you learn something durable that the code does not already state:

    entire brain remember "<memory>" --path <category.subcategory.type> --json

Categories are architecture, constraints, preferences, project and workflow.
Omitting --path classifies the memory for you, which requires a supported coding
agent on PATH. Over MCP the same write is the brain_remember tool, which
requires path. Retrieve with recall, and re-check anchors with verify.

Use Brain entities history to connect code changes to earlier checkpoints and
sessions. Use Brain memory-informed review and workspace
capabilities when relevant. Brain semantic answers refer to a stored index, which
may differ from current working-tree source.

Use Brain's code inspection tools for relevant code questions.

Read focused source around useful locations before editing. Check related contracts

# Entire repository agent guide — Brain

Use Brain for task context and retained knowledge. Begin substantive tasks needing
orientation with:

    entire brain brief "<task>" --json

Run it before deciding the task does not need it: what the brief adds is the part
you do not already know about.

Questions about why something is the way it is, what was decided, or what was
tried before are answered by durable memories. Retrieve them directly; the brief's
memories section is a sample, not the search:

    entire brain recall "<question>" --json

recall ranks decisions, rejected approaches, invariants and gotchas first. query
mixes memories with history and documentation and can rank documentation above the
recorded decision.

Reuse useful code locations from the brief. Use Brain retrieval for previous
decisions, attempts, documentation, and durable memories - Brain's episodic record
of what was decided, what went wrong before, and what must stay true. Record one
when you learn something durable that the code does not already state:

    entire brain remember "<memory>" --path <category.subcategory.type> --json

Categories are architecture, constraints, preferences, project and workflow.
Omitting --path classifies the memory for you, which requires a supported coding
agent on PATH. Over MCP the same write is the brain_remember tool, which
requires path. Retrieve with recall, and re-check anchors with verify.

Use Brain entities history to connect code changes to earlier checkpoints and
sessions. Use Brain memory-informed review and workspace
capabilities when relevant. Brain semantic answers refer to a stored index, which
may differ from current working-tree source.

Use Brain's code inspection tools for relevant code questions.

Read focused source around useful locations before editing. Check related contracts

# Road to v1

Unshipped work only. [Owner requirement](../specs/REQ-DX-V1.md), [scoped model and prior art](../architecture/polyglot-v1.md).

Canonical `ecosystem/name` references, historical tag ownership, one tag and release per package, per-distribution publish ordering and the redacted failure tail have shipped. [ADR 12](../adr/0012-canonical-distribution-release-ownership.md) records them.

## Scope and guardrails

- Rust/Cargo, npm/pnpm and Python/PyPI, including napi-rs layouts. Co-located Cargo/Maturin is after v1; separate-directory Cargo and Python packages are supported. Go and NuGet are architecture examples only.
- Native tools and CI own building, packing and authentication. No universal package manager, build scheduler, public plugin platform or cross-registry transaction.
- Committed release authority and provider-observed recovery with no execution journal. Only `execute` receives registry secrets; the repo has no GitHub Environment or reviewer gate.
- Each implementation PR updates the affected specs, tests and docs, with one changeset per independent user-facing topic.

## Open work

| Item | State |
| --- | --- |
| Co-located Cargo/Maturin | After v1. Both a static and a dynamic Python version fail with E007. |
| Production-path registry tests for Cargo and PyPI | The tests drive the publisher argv directly and bypass registry binding and observation. A path through binding is blocked because `registry_endpoint.rs` rejects non-https URLs, loopback included. Decide the approach, then build it or drop it. npm already goes through the real adapter. |
| Native fixture evidence | Cargo and napi clean install and load, mixed workspaces and packed pnpm metadata are not recorded as a verification matrix. |
| First-release onboarding time | The goal of under ten minutes from a fresh repo to a first published release has not been measured. |
| Release target table | `matrix.rs` carries its own 18-triple table instead of reading rustc's target facts. |

## Owner decisions still open

- Private and HTML-only PyPI indexes: [publishing](../publishing.md) says they need explicit support.
- npm channel promotion. Prereleases already publish under their own dist-tag.
- Universal checksums, and wrapper bump severity.
- Inferred-only releases in managed CI: `status` warns, but whether inference may open the release PR is an ADR 2 question.
- Release-commit provenance: ADR 2 documents the unkeyed digest.
- Whether to add a workspace-wide check for discarded source errors. The lints deny `let_underscore_must_use`, `let_underscore_untyped` and `map_err_ignore`.
- npm JSON layout normalization, and the scope of napi `.node` attestation.
- External items: rust-cache pin, bot-PR check policy, token rotation and the retired-crate migration notices.

## After 1.0

OIDC trusted publishing ([plan](OIDC-TRUSTED-PUBLISHING.md)), `cargo-semver-checks` on the promised surfaces (schema output, config and report formats), and a review of the remaining `expect` calls.
# REQ-DX-V1: world-class release DX and correctness for v1

Stakeholder: Callisto owner (sole maintainer); users releasing Rust, npm (incl. napi-rs) and Python monorepos.

Status: open. The command surface and release machinery exist; [the roadmap](../projects/ROAD-TO-V1.md) lists the verification and onboarding work that remains. Real local npm, Cargo and PyPI tests exist; the Cargo and PyPI ones drive the publisher directly and do not cover registry binding or observation.

Why: Callisto's release engine is rigorous but its surface is confusing and its setup is heavy. Goal: a new repo goes from `callisto init` to its first published release in under 10 minutes, with one obvious release command and no known correctness bugs.

## Decided by the owner

- The main verb is `release`. Flow: `add` → `version` → `release`.
- `callisto release` publishes every package whose version has no release yet: registry publish, tag, forge release. `--dry-run` previews it on any branch.
- User-facing commands shown in `--help`: init, add, status, version, release, pre, snapshot, completions. Plumbing stays callable but hidden.
- `add` keeps both modes: interactive wizard on a TTY, flags for automation, clear error with the needed flags when neither.
- Breaking changes are fine pre-1.0; no external users.
- Current implementation scope is Rust/Cargo, npm/pnpm (including napi-rs) and Python/PyPI. Keep architecture room for Go and C#/.NET/NuGet without implementing those adapters now.
- Prefer canonical ecosystem-qualified references and deliberate legacy migration over collision-triggered identity magic. Release ownership, native distribution identity, version authority and effects are separate responsibilities; the detailed proposal is [the scoped model](../architecture/polyglot-v1.md).
- Do not build a universal package manager, build scheduler, cross-language inference engine or persisted execution journal. Native tools/CI own compilation, packing and authentication.

## Done when

- `callisto --help` lists exactly the 8 user commands; each has one plain-language line.
- `callisto release --dry-run` with no flags prints the full plan on any branch; `callisto release` with no flags performs it locally with credentials in the environment.
- The CI split (plan → build → execute across jobs) works through `release` flags or hidden subcommands, and callisto's own workflow uses them.
- `publish`, `plan-publish`, `tag`, `filter-plan` are removed; one plan implementation serves preview and execution and includes every check listed above.
- Text output uses colour/tables on a TTY, plain text when piped or `NO_COLOR` is set, no schema versions in text; `status` shows cascaded bumps.
- A verified defect is fixed with regression coverage across affected siblings. CI runs the shipped runtime behavior; no shipped Cargo feature variants. The real local npm/Cargo/PyPI tests fail, not skip, under CI when a tool is missing, and production binding/observation paths are checked separately.
- `callisto init` detects ecosystems/packages, asks only intent (fixed vs independent; release artifacts if binaries exist), writes minimal config, and can write a GitHub workflow using `callisto-action` of <= 40 lines; a non-interactive mode exists.
- Supported fixtures cover separate native packages, and dual Cargo/npm outputs. Native dependency ranges/names, all affected lockfiles and built distribution metadata agree after versioning.
